clue.text: Batrachian mansion

parts.note: batrachian means of frogs and toads, so this is the stately home of the toad in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows

explanation.walkthrough: Batrachian is the zoological word for frogs and toads; the mansion is Mr Toad's grand house in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Grahame's children's novel the wealthy amphibian lives in a riverside manor of that name.

clue.text: Catch up-check up

explanation.surface: A terse line about catching up and checking up, as if from a to-do list.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a rival in a race is to draw level and go by; to inspect and repair a machine thoroughly is a full service.

clue.text: Point of return for the unsuccessful designer

definitions.text: Point of return for the unsuccessful designer

parts.words: Point of return for the unsuccessful designer
parts.note: a designer whose plan fails must go back and start again at the sloping desk where plans are first sketched

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'back to the square one of design' is 'back to the drawing board', said of any plan that has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloped desk on which plans are first drafted is where a failed scheme is restarted, as the idiom says.

clue.text: League of Five Hundred leave the pleasures of the primrose path

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for five hundred is told to leave, so it drops out of the longer word

parts.words: the pleasures of the primrose path
parts.note: the primrose path is a life of pleasure, and its amorous trifling is dalliance
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A society of five hundred members renounces a life of easy pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The primrose path of dalliance' is Ophelia's phrase in Hamlet; take D (500) out of DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a formal union of parties, the same as a confederation or pact.

clue.text: Rhine maiden

parts.note: the siren of German legend who sat on a rock above the river and lured boatmen to their deaths

explanation.definitionFit: In German folklore and Heine's poem, a siren on a rock by the river who sings sailors to their doom.

clue.text: Though the queen did nothing, he deserted her

definitions.text: Though the queen did nothing, he deserted her

parts.words: Though the queen did nothing, he deserted her
parts.note: the queen is Dido of Carthage, whose name splits as DID plus O, nothing; the Trojan hero who left her is meant

explanation.surface: A lament for a blameless queen abandoned by her lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did nothing' spells the queen's name, DID + O = DIDO; in Virgil's Aeneid the Trojan hero abandons Dido of Carthage to found Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's epic the Trojan prince leaves Carthage and its queen at the gods' command.

clue.text: One of three fairy gifts

parts.note: in fairy tales a magical being often grants the hero three of these desires

explanation.definitionFit: Fairy godmothers and genies traditionally grant three desires to the lucky mortal.

clue.text: Bold, loud, like Van Gogh

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
the painter Van Gogh famously cut off part of his ear, so he was without one

explanation.surface: A description of a painter as bold, brash and in the manner of Van Gogh.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and brave both describe someone without fear.

clue.text: Profitable work for the cuckoo, every hour on the hour

definitions.text: Profitable work for the cuckoo, every hour on the hour

parts.words: Profitable work for the cuckoo, every hour on the hour
parts.note: a cuckoo clock's bird comes out at each hour, and extra hours of paid work are hours beyond the normal day

explanation.surface: A cuckoo clock's bird pops out each hour, as though clocking up paid hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoo in a clock 'works' at each hour as it strikes; paid extra hours are this, and the bird is out exactly when the hour is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra hours worked beyond the normal day are paid at a higher rate.

clue.text: A girl to rave about !

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters of rave are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a girl worth raving over.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's first name.

clue.text: It helps the coward to fly, no doubt

definitions.text: It helps the coward to fly, no doubt

parts.words: It helps the coward to fly, no doubt
parts.note: a feather helps a bird fly, and a coward flies in the sense of runs away; the pale plume is the badge of cowardice

explanation.surface: A wry remark that something aids a coward's flight.
explanation.walkthrough: A white plume was handed to men thought cowards; 'fly' means both take wing, as a feather helps, and flee.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale plume is the traditional emblem of cowardice, once handed to men who would not fight.

clue.text: Complete diet is not to be found in a cul-de-sac

definitions.text: not to be found in a cul-de-sac
definitions.note: a phrase describing a road, standing for the road itself

parts.note: thorough means complete or utter
fare is food, the diet one eats

explanation.surface: A full diet cannot be got in a dead-end street.
explanation.walkthrough: A cul-de-sac is a dead end, so signs say 'No ...' for it: the open through-road is what it lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street has no through-road, which is why such roads are signed 'No' plus this word.

clue.text: The gun with which to make a break

definitions.text: with which to make a break

explanation.surface: A gun used to make a break for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A big gun is old artillery; in billiards a shot striking both other balls is a scoring stroke used to build a break.

clue.text: Place comfortably — as a candle in its holder ?

definitions.text: as a candle in its holder

explanation.surface: Settling something snugly, as a candle sits in its holder.
explanation.walkthrough: A sconce is a wall bracket for a candle; split the answer as EN SCONCE, French for 'in sconce'.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle snugly is to install oneself cosily; split, it reads 'in sconce', a sconce being a wall candle-bracket.

clue.text: What makes the whale wail ?

parts.note: the whale's thick fat layer shares its name with a verb meaning to sob noisily

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a whale cry.
explanation.walkthrough: The fat of a whale shares its spelling with a verb meaning to weep noisily, so it both is the whale and makes it 'wail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whale fat is the same word as the verb for crying loudly.

clue.text: Suit for young buffers ?

parts.note: buffers here are people in the buff, naked; the suit a baby wears is bare skin

explanation.surface: A tailor's line about clothes for young old fogeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old buffer' suggests elderly men, but here buffers are those in the buff; the 'birthday suit' is nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: One's 'birthday suit' is bare skin, as worn at birth.

clue.text: Shoots the odds at parties

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a horse race
a rout is an old word for a large evening party

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on the odds at social gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' looks like a verb (fires) but is the noun for new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Young growths on a plant are new shoots.

clue.text: Veto the portion discovered under the ruins of Ophir

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that is discovered under another is placed after it
the ancient city's name lies in ruins, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bit is a portion or piece

explanation.surface: An archaeologist bans a find unearthed at the ancient site of Ophir.
explanation.walkthrough: Ophir is the biblical land of gold; 'the ruins of' rearranges OPHIR to PROHI, and 'discovered under' puts BIT below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to forbid or ban.

clue.text: Scientific speculator

parts.note: a speculator here is one who speculates in ideas, not money: someone who forms hypotheses

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who frames hypotheses rather than testing them is a man of ideas in science.

clue.text: A bob to a quid it'll make you almost laugh

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S in British money before 1971
nicker is British slang for a pound, as is quid

explanation.surface: A bet of a shilling against a pound that it will make you laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob, quid and nicker are British slang: a shilling and a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppressed half-laugh is a giggle or snigger, short of laughing outright.

clue.text: Worldly effect of love

parts.note: the saying goes that love makes the world go round, so its effect on the world is turning

explanation.surface: A remark on what love does to the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love makes the world go round': its effect on the world is spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Going round is spinning on an axis, as the earth does daily.

clue.text: Head of Russian territory leaves for the Peninsula

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is the one that goes
leaves means departs, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: Siberia is the vast Russian territory east of the Urals

explanation.surface: A Russian leader quits his territory for the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of ... leaves' removes the S from SIBERIA; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal share the Iberian peninsula, anciently called by this name.

clue.text: One goes right ' wild at these parties!

indicators.note: going wild signals the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone goes wild at these riotous parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, drunken revels are debauched parties.

clue.text: Othello's " ocular proof "

parts.note: in Shakespeare's play Othello demands visible proof of Desdemona's guilt, and Iago supplies her strawberry-spotted token

explanation.walkthrough: Othello demands 'the ocular proof' of Desdemona's infidelity; Iago plants her strawberry-embroidered handkerchief on Cassio.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy the embroidered token Desdemona drops is the visible evidence Iago uses.

clue.text: " Beauty's self she is "

parts.note: a line quoted from a poem on an unclothed woman, beauty itself with nothing added

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation praises a woman who is beauty itself, needing no clothes or adornment.
explanation.definitionFit: An unclothed figure, as in art, is beauty unadorned.

clue.text: There's nothing wet in having peculiar ideas

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase has the answer in it, so the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone with odd ideas is anything but soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' suggests a feeble person, but here it is literal: dry; the letters run across peculiAR IDeas.
explanation.definitionFit: Land with no moisture at all is dry, desert-like.

clue.text: Eye of newt for instance could tie David in knots

indicators.note: tied in knots means twisted up, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A witch's ingredient that could tie a man called David in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye of newt is one of the witches' ingredients in Macbeth, added to the cauldron.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put into a brew or food to change it is an ingredient added in, like the witches' eye of newt.

clue.text: Withdraws to secluded spots

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws to quiet hideaways.
explanation.definitionFit: An army pulls back when it falls back; quiet havens are hideaways one goes to.
